Colorectal distension (CRD) was used to assess the visceral sensitivity of the WKY rat compared to normosensitive Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats. Visceral sensitivity was quantified by measuring visceromotor responses (VMR), which are abdominal muscle contractions in response to CRD, and by assessing the behavioral response to CRD. WKY rats exhibited a heightened VMR to CRD compared to SD rats, indicating increased visceral sensitivity. Administration of RS-127445 significantly reduced the VMR in WKY rats, bringing it closer to levels observed in SD rats. This suggests that 5-HT(2B) receptors play a significant role in modulating visceral hypersensitivity in this stress-sensitive model. Additionally, behavioral responses to CRD were also attenuated by RS-127445 in WKY rats, further supporting the involvement of 5-HT(2B) receptors in the modulation of visceral pain. The discovery of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) in 2003 in families with familial hypercholesterolemia (HF) later generated the development of pharmacological strategies in order to inhibit this protein. The first of these, alirocumab, was approved in the United States in 2015, and the second, evolocumab, in 2015. The purpose of this review is to discuss the characteristics of PCSK9 inhibitors, their effects on LDL-c, and their implications in the treatment of hypercholesterolemia.
